messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 - ArchonWorks (privnet) NLB tg-archon-prod showing sustained 5xx >40% across az-a/az-b. Impact: customer traffic errors. Runbook: privnet-nlb-response.

miguel_oncall: i'm on pager. confirm Archon is private VPC with dedicated pool and NAT instances in the path? taking lead.

leah_ops: confirmed. NLB -> ALB -> private targets. CloudWatch shows surge coincident with NAT conntrack exhaustion logs on nat-hosts. SG logs show RST from nat instances for established flows.

sam_net: looking at NLB target health: many targets flapping 503. ALB target group draining then re-registering. hypothesis: conntrack exhaustion on NAT causes upstream resets.

miguel_oncall: immediate mitigations we can do: 1) move a portion of traffic off priv zone to our hosted-fallback cluster 2) temporarily widen conntrack on NAT 3) blackhole problematic subnet ranges. which do we want first?

jess_product: archon_csm on the line and gave provisional approval for routing change to fallback for up to 30m. they prefer partial shift first.

sam_net: applying weighted failover via Route53 private zone. change: set archon.priv -> primary weight 70, fallback 30. TTL 60s to speed convergence.

sam_net: command used:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZPVT1234 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.archon.priv","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"fallback","Weight":30,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.12.34.56"}]}}]}'
```

miguel_oncall: DNS change done. within 90s we see traffic shift. overall 5xx rate dropped: 42% -> 18% in ~2m.

neteng: while DNS propagates, preparing conntrack mitigation. increasing nf_conntrack max on NAT hosts and restarting conntrack cleanup service.

leah_ops: running conntrack -L shows many TIME_WAIT + ESTABLISHED entries to backend ports. capturing pcap for sample flows and collecting ALB access logs for error codes.

neteng: conntrack tune applied: sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288 and enabled net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=86400. monitoring.

miguel_oncall: after conntrack bump, NAT RSTs reduced. 5xx now 6% but still clustered to particular target subnets. suggestion: drain those subnets from target group and let autoscale replace.

sam_net: deregistered targets in subnet 10.2.5.0/24 from tg-archon-prod and set target-group slow_start to 30s. started 4 replacement instances in dedicated pool.

leah_ops: grabbing traces for impacted sessions to see if specific endpoints cause long-lived connections. initial sample shows many long polling websocket-style connections leading to conntrack pressure.

archon_csm: Archon on call appreciates quick action. they report partial recovery for some tenants, a subset still seeing intermittent failures.

sre-bot: Incident update: mitigation = Route53 weighted shift (30% fallback), nf_conntrack increase on NAT hosts, targeted target deregistration on subnet 10.2.5. Monitoring for 15m window.

miguel_oncall: plan for next steps: if 5xx <5% for 15m keep fallback at 30% and start gradual rollback to primary 85% over 30m. if spike returns, full failover to hosted fallback and schedule postmortem with Archon.

leah_ops: taking point for handoff at 15:40 UTC. i'll continue monitoring metrics, coordinate with neteng for any further conntrack tuning, and own post-incident action items: conntrack tuning permanence, consider NAT autoscaling, and ALB target timeout alignment with client long polls.

miguel_oncall: handing over. reachable if needed. good job team. :thumbsup:

leah_ops: acknowledged. leaving thread open for monitoring window; will post final resolution or escalate if regression.

sre-bot: Incident remains P1 - next automated update scheduled in 15 minutes or on state change.
